matches.rationale: Findings 4 and 5 both directly identify that Theorem 2.3's claimed swap/complex-conjugation description only works when the relevant Hodge component has dimension ≤1, and fails (is underdetermined) for higher-dimensional components such as the quintic threefold's 101-dimensional piece — exactly the mechanism described in the ground truth. Findings 1–3 address different, downstream or unrelated issues (a sign/antilinearity problem in Corollary 2.7, its concrete instance in Example 2.8, and a homological degree shift in Section 2.1) rather than the dimension-generality flaw itself.

pred_verdicts.rationale: Identifies a plausible sign/antilinearity inconsistency in Corollary 2.7 via Lean, but this is a distinct symptom (sign error) rather than the dimension-generality flaw of Theorem 2.3 recorded in the ground truth.
Explicitly states it is 'the concrete instance of the Corollary 2.7 sign error' found in pred_id 1, so it reports the same defect.
Points to a genuine but unrelated homological-degree mismatch in the long exact sequence of Section 2.1, not part of the listed ground truth defect.
Correctly identifies that Theorem 2.3's claim fails to uniquely determine the representative when the Hodge component dimension exceeds 1, matching the ground truth mechanism.
Pinpoints the exact non-sequitur in the proof of Theorem 2.3 where a single scalar equation cannot determine a higher-dimensional component, matching the ground truth's stated flaw.
